question: Naphthalene balls used to repel moths and other insects are obtained from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**coal tar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Naphthalene balls are made from coal tar.**
 
• **Moths and other insects are repelled by naphthalene balls**.
 
• The deadly **white solid naphthalene,** which **has a pungent odour**, is frequently employed as a moth repellant.
 
• Coal gas contains **flammable gases.**
 
• **Petroleum or coal tar can be used to make naphthalene.**
 
• Coal tar distillation and fractionation are the most typical production processes.
 
• The **naphthalene** is subsequently purified by **fractionation, decolourization, and crystallisation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Coke **​

 
 
• **Coke is produced by heating coal or oil without the presence of air**, which is a **damaging distillation process**.
 
• Coke is a grey, hard, and porous fuel with a high carbon content and minimal impurities.
 
 
 
• **Coal gas**
 
 
• ​**A fuel comprised of hydrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide known as coal gas **is created through destructive distillation, which is the continuous heating of bituminous coal without the presence of air.
 
• With various amounts of other elements including **hydrogen, sulphur, oxygen, and nitrogen, coal is mostly composed of carbon.**
 
 
 
• **Coal**
 
 
• **One of the most practical fossil fuels is coal. **
 
• A combination of gases that were once utilised for lighting and heating and obtained by the destructive distillation of coal.
 
• The majority of its **components are hydrocarbons and carbon**, both of which contain **energy that can be released when burned (burning).**
